answer:
### The brand that rolled out the most SUV models in 2014 (per J.D. Power)

| Brand | 2014 SUV models mentioned in J.D. Power’s “New Vehicle Releases” list |
|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Chevrolet** | **3** – **Equinox**, **Suburban**, **Tahoe** |
| Ford | 1 – **Edge** |
| GMC | 2 – **Terrain**, **Yukon** |
| Cadillac | 1 – **Escalade** |
| Dodge | 1 – **Grand Caravan** (classified as a minivan/compact‑SUV‑style) |
| Jeep | 0 – no new SUV listed for 2014 in the JD‑Power list |
| Nissan | 1 – **FJ Cruiser** |
| Lincoln | 1 – **MKX** |
| Honda | 1 – **Ridgeline** |
| Toyota | 1 – **FJ Cruiser** (Toyota also has the **Highlander**, but the list highlights the **FJ Cruiser** as the 2014 SUV roll‑out) |
| Volkswagen | 0 – no new SUV listed for 2014 in the JD‑Power list |

**Answer:** **Chevrolet**.  
Chevrolet is the only manufacturer that had three distinct SUV models referenced in J.D. Power’s 2014 new‑vehicle release information, whereas other brands rolled out one or two at most.

Title: Top-Ranked Cars, Trucks and SUVs in the J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**

In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**

The entry-level Accent is the most appealing Small Car in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_, ranked higher than the Ford Fiesta and Chevrolet Sonic. For 2014, Hyundai added standard features, improved the car's voice-recognition Bluetooth system, and installed new upgrades for upper trim levels.
**2014 Kia Soul**
Redesigned for 2014, the Kia Soul is the highest-ranked Compact Multi-Purpose Vehicle in terms of appeal. Larger and more refined than it was before, the latest version of the Soul offers modern technology and practicality wrapped up in a unique package.
**2014 Land Rover Range Rover**
Among the most appealing models regardless of price, the Land Rover Range Rover is the highest-ranked model in the Large Premium SUV category in the _2014 APEAL Study_. This year, a new supercharged V-6 engine replaced last year's standard V-8 engine, LED headlights are standard, adaptive cruise control is less expensive, and Autobiography models gained equipment.
**2014 Mazda 6**
Redesigned this year, the Mazda 6 is the most appealing Midsize Car for 2014, ahead of the Kia Optima and Hyundai Sonata. Offered only with a 4-cylinder engine, the Mazda 6 can be optioned with several technologies commonly available only on more expensive vehicles.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class**
Among Midsize Premium Cars, the Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class ranks as the most appealing model, ahead of the Audi A7 and Audi A6. For 2014, Mercedes added 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard equipment for the performance-tuned CLS63 AMG, and debuted a higher-performance CLS63 AMG S-Model.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz S-Class**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 S-Class ties with the Audi A8 as the most appealing Large Premium Car in the latest _J.D. Power APEAL Study_. Four variants, including two high-performance AMG models, range in price from $94,000 to $222,000. Next-generation infotainment and autonomous safety technologies highlight the newest family of S-Class models.
**2014 Mini Countryman**

Ranking higher than the Buick Encore and Volkswagen Tiguan, the Mini Countryman is the most appealing Small SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_. New John Cooper Works appearance packages debuted this past year, and Mini made minor equipment changes, including the addition of a standard 3-passenger rear bench seat, replacing the previous bucket seats.
**2014 Nissan Quest**
According to the _2014 APEAL Study_, Nissan Quest owners like their minivans, and this model ranks higher than the popular Honda Odyssey and Toyota Sienna for overall appeal in 2014. Aside from new colors, no changes were made this year.
**2014 Nissan Rogue**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 Nissan Rogue receives an award for ranking highest among Compact SUVs in the _2014 APEAL Study_, ahead of the Ford Escape and Jeep Cherokee. It is one of two models in its class to offer 7-passenger seating, and is available with numerous infotainment and safety technologies.
**2014 Porsche 911**
The multitude of Porsche 911 variants collectively ranks highest for vehicle appeal among Midsize Premium Sporty Cars. This year, Targa, Turbo, and GT3 versions joined the 911 lineup.
**2014 Porsche Boxster**
The Porsche Boxster ranks higher than the Porsche Cayman and Nissan 370Z among Compact Premium Sporty Cars in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_. One year following a complete redesign, the Boxster received few changes.
**2014 Porsche Cayenne**
Among Premium Midsize SUVs, the Porsche Cayenne ranks higher than do the BMW X5 and redesigned Land Rover Range Rover Sport. For 2014, a new Platinum Edition debuted at the lower end of the range while a high-performance Turbo S variant arrived as a range-topping flagship model.
**2014 Toyota Highlander**
Redesigned for 2014, the Toyota Highlander is the highest-ranked Midsize SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_, followed by the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The Highlander offers seating for up to 8 people, and a choice between a 4-cylinder, V-6, or gas-electric hybrid powertrains.

**2014 Volkswagen GTI**
Compact Sporty Car buyers rate their Volkswagen GTIs higher in terms of appeal than do people purchasing the Hyundai Veloster and Mini Cooper. In advance of a redesigned 2015 model, the 2014 GTI was offered only as a 5-door hatchback.

**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**
texts.1:

**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Title: JD Power and LMC Automotive Forecast October 2014 - JD Power
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6
**WESTLAKE VILLAGE, Calif.: 27 October 2014** — New-vehicle retail sales are expected to reach their highest level for the month of October since 2004, according to a monthly sales forecast developed jointly by JD Power and LMC Automotive.
**Retail Light-Vehicle Sales**
New-vehicle retail sales in October 2014 are projected to come in at 1.1 million units, a 6 percent increase, compared with October 2013. The retail seasonally adjusted annualized rate (SAAR) in October is expected to be 13.6 million units, 0.7 million units stronger than October 2013. Retail transactions are the most accurate measure of true underlying consumer demand for new vehicles.
**U.S. Retail SAAR—October 2013 to October 2014**
**(in millions of units)**
**Source: _Power Information Network® (PIN)_ from JD Power**
“The industry continues to demonstrate strong sales growth and robust transaction prices, resulting in another record-breaking month for industry consumer spending,” said John Humphrey, senior vice president of the global automotive practice at JD Power.
JD Power expects consumer spending on new vehicles to exceed $32.5 billion in October, the highest level for the month of October since 2013 when consumer spending reached $30.7 billion.
In addition to overall better economic conditions, Humphrey said growth in retail sales and higher transaction prices are in part due to increasing consumer adoption of longer-term financing which makes purchases more affordable from a monthly payment perspective. Nearly one-third (32.6%) of all vehicles sold in October 2014 are financed with a term of 72 months or longer, tying the record set in July 2014.
**Total Light-Vehicle Sales**
Total light-vehicle sales in October 2014 are expected to reach 1.27 million units, a 6 percent increase from October 2013. Fleet volume is expected to be 203,000 units, or 16 percent of total light-vehicle sales.
**JD Power and LMC Automotive U.S. Sales and SAAR Comparisons**

October 2014 1 September 2014 October 2013  
New-Vehicle Retail Sales 1,068,400 units
(6% higher than October 2013)1,013,926 units 1,012,466 units  
Total Vehicle Sales 1,271,500 units
(6% higher than October 2013)1,243,239 units 1,205,193 units  
Retail SAAR 13.6 million units 13.6 million units 12.9 million units  
Total SAAR 16.3 million units 16.4 million units 15.3 million units
1 Figures cited for October 2014 are forecasted based on the first 16 selling days of the month.
**Sales Outlook**
LMC Automotive is holding its 2014 U.S. light-vehicle retail sales forecast at 13.6 million units and total light-vehicle sales forecast at 16.4 million units. SUV sales have increased 12 percent in 2014 compared with 2013, while total new-vehicle sales have increased 5 percent for the same period. SUVs are expected to account for 34 percent of the light-vehicle market in 2014, up from 32 percent in 2013.
“The current environment of the auto industry is one of strength and stability, with the second half of the year at a 16.6 million-unit pace, more than making up for the 16.1 million unit level in the first half of 2014,” said Jeff Schuster, senior vice president of forecasting at LMC Automotive. “The market is clearly seeing a second wave of SUV popularity—with a wide variety of choices across the size spectrum—that will likely dominate market share for the foreseeable future.”
**North American Production**

Following very strong sales in August that reduced a significant amount of inventory, North American production in September increased 3.3 percent versus last year, resulting in an increase of over 1.4 million units from September 2013. With the increase in September, production in the third quarter totaled 4.1 million units, a 7.2 percent volume increase, compared with the third quarter of 2013 and the highest third quarter total on record. Compact SUVs experienced the largest volume growth in the third quarter, up more than 90,000 units, compared with the same period in 2013.
LMC Automotive’s North American production forecast in 2014 remains at 16.8 million units, a 4 percent increase from 16.2 million units in 2013. North American production for 2015 is forecast to eclipse the 17 million-unit mark, with capacity utilization continuing to run at or above the 90 percent level.
Vehicle inventory at the end of September was at a 64-day supply, up from 56 days at the end of August.

### About JD Power
JD Power is a global marketing information services company providing performance improvement, social media and customer satisfaction insights and solutions. The company’s quality and satisfaction measurements are based on responses from millions of consumers annually. Headquartered in Westlake Village, Calif., JD Power has offices in North/South America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information on car reviews and ratings, car insurance, health insurance, cell phone ratings, and more, please visit www.JDPower.com. JD Power is a business unit of McGraw Hill Financial.

### About McGraw Hill Financial
McGraw Hill Financial is a leading financial intelligence company providing the global capital and commodity markets with independent benchmarks, credit ratings, portfolio and enterprise risk solutions, and analytics. The Company’s iconic brands include Standard & Poor’s Ratings Services, S&P Capital IQ, S&P Dow Jones Indices, Platts, CRISIL and JD Power. The Company has approximately 18,000 employees in 30 countries. Additional information is available at www.mhfi.com.

### About LMC Automotive
LMC Automotive is the premier supplier of automotive forecasts and intelligence to an extensive client base of automotive manufacturer, component supplier, logistics and distribution companies, as well as financial and government institutions around the world. LMC’s global forecasting services encompass automotive sales, production and powertrain expertise, as well as advisory capability. LMC Automotive has locations in the United States, the UK, France, Germany, China Japan and Thailand and is part of the Oxford, UK-based LMC group, the global leader in economic and business consultancy for the agribusiness sector. For more information please visit www.lmc-auto.com.

*   **Honda won the 2026 U.S. News & World Report "Best Car Brand" award for the fifth consecutive year.**  
*   **Honda announced that it joined Carbon by Indigo, a leading program to help farmers across the U.S. adopt regenerative agriculture practices to improve soil health, capture carbon and increase their profitability.**

## **2025**
*   **Honda announced a new multi-year partnership, serving as the Exclusive Automotive Partner and Official Vehicle of USA Hockey, the title sponsor of the USA Hockey Sled National Championships and supporting USA Hockey during the Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games Milano Cortina 2026.**

October*   **Honda Racing Corporation (HRC US) announced plans to debut "Formula R" – the first-ever consumer engine oil line, available starting in spring 2026.**  
*   Honda unveiled prototypes at the Japan Mobility Show 2025, including the Honda Ø α (alpha) EV SUV, the EV OUTLIER motorcycle concept and the Super-ONE compact EV.  
*   Honda Motor announced an investment in OMC Power Private Limited (OMC Power) with an aim to launch a leasing business for an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) device using the Honda Mobile Power Pack e: swappable battery, starting in January 2026.

CR-V sales started in Japan and quickly expanded around the world, now sold in approximately 150 countries, with cumulative global sales exceeding 15 million units*. CR-V surpassed 400,000 units for the second straight year in 2025 – an all-time best sales record in the U.S. The CR-V is built at the Honda East Liberty Plant in Ohio and the Indiana Auto Plant, using domestic and globally made parts.  
*   **Honda Research Institute USA, Inc. (HRI-US) announced a $2.6 million investment for a new Advanced Materials Science Lab in Ohio, to support research and innovation for future Honda technologies.**  
*   Moto Honda da Amazonia Ltda. (HAD), Honda subsidiary for the production and sales of motorcycles and power products in Brazil, announced plans to invest approximately 1.6 billion reals from 2026 to 2029 in its plant in Manaus to meet the growing demand in Brazil’s motorcycle market.  
*   **Honda and the Honda USA Foundation kicked off their annual funding cycle for eligible nonprofit organizations and schools to apply for grant awards supporting high-impact programs that align with the company's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) vision to help people fulfill their life's potential.**

**WESTLAKE VILLAGE, Calif.: 27 October 2014** — New-vehicle retail sales are expected to reach their highest level for the month of October since 2004, according to a monthly sales forecast developed jointly by JD Power and LMC Automotive.
**Retail Light-Vehicle Sales**
New-vehicle retail sales in October 2014 are projected to come in at 1.1 million units, a 6 percent increase, compared with October 2013. The retail seasonally adjusted annualized rate (SAAR) in October is expected to be 13.6 million units, 0.7 million units stronger than October 2013. Retail transactions are the most accurate measure of true underlying consumer demand for new vehicles.
**U.S. Retail SAAR—October 2013 to October 2014**
**(in millions of units)**
**Source: _Power Information Network® (PIN)_ from JD Power**
“The industry continues to demonstrate strong sales growth and robust transaction prices, resulting in another record-breaking month for industry consumer spending,” said John Humphrey, senior vice president of the global automotive practice at JD Power.
JD Power expects consumer spending on new vehicles to exceed $32.5 billion in October, the highest level for the month of October since 2013 when consumer spending reached $30.7 billion.
In addition to overall better economic conditions, Humphrey said growth in retail sales and higher transaction prices are in part due to increasing consumer adoption of longer-term financing which makes purchases more affordable from a monthly payment perspective. Nearly one-third (32.6%) of all vehicles sold in October 2014 are financed with a term of 72 months or longer, tying the record set in July 2014.
**Total Light-Vehicle Sales**
Total light-vehicle sales in October 2014 are expected to reach 1.27 million units, a 6 percent increase from October 2013. Fleet volume is expected to be 203,000 units, or 16 percent of total light-vehicle sales.
**JD Power and LMC Automotive U.S. Sales and SAAR Comparisons**

SUV sales have increased 12 percent in 2014 compared with 2013, while total new-vehicle sales have increased 5 percent for the same period. SUVs are expected to account for 34 percent of the light-vehicle market in 2014, up from 32 percent in 2013.
“The current environment of the auto industry is one of strength and stability, with the second half of the year at a 16.6 million-unit pace, more than making up for the 16.1 million unit level in the first half of 2014,” said Jeff Schuster, senior vice president of forecasting at LMC Automotive. “The market is clearly seeing a second wave of SUV popularity—with a wide variety of choices across the size spectrum—that will likely dominate market share for the foreseeable future.”

texts.2:
Following very strong sales in August that reduced a significant amount of inventory, North American production in September increased 3.3 percent versus last year, resulting in an increase of over 1.4 million units from September 2013. With the increase in September, production in the third quarter totaled 4.1 million units, a 7.2 percent volume increase, compared with the third quarter of 2013 and the highest third quarter total on record. Compact SUVs experienced the largest volume growth in the third quarter, up more than 90,000 units, compared with the same period in 2013.
LMC Automotive’s North American production forecast in 2014 remains at 16.8 million units, a 4 percent increase from 16.2 million units in 2013. North American production for 2015 is forecast to eclipse the 17 million-unit mark, with capacity utilization continuing to run at or above the 90 percent level.
Vehicle inventory at the end of September was at a 64-day supply, up from 56 days at the end of August.

The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**

In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**

The entry-level Accent is the most appealing Small Car in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_, ranked higher than the Ford Fiesta and Chevrolet Sonic. For 2014, Hyundai added standard features, improved the car's voice-recognition Bluetooth system, and installed new upgrades for upper trim levels.
**2014 Kia Soul**
Redesigned for 2014, the Kia Soul is the highest-ranked Compact Multi-Purpose Vehicle in terms of appeal. Larger and more refined than it was before, the latest version of the Soul offers modern technology and practicality wrapped up in a unique package.
**2014 Land Rover Range Rover**
Among the most appealing models regardless of price, the Land Rover Range Rover is the highest-ranked model in the Large Premium SUV category in the _2014 APEAL Study_. This year, a new supercharged V-6 engine replaced last year's standard V-8 engine, LED headlights are standard, adaptive cruise control is less expensive, and Autobiography models gained equipment.
**2014 Mazda 6**
Redesigned this year, the Mazda 6 is the most appealing Midsize Car for 2014, ahead of the Kia Optima and Hyundai Sonata. Offered only with a 4-cylinder engine, the Mazda 6 can be optioned with several technologies commonly available only on more expensive vehicles.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class**
Among Midsize Premium Cars, the Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class ranks as the most appealing model, ahead of the Audi A7 and Audi A6. For 2014, Mercedes added 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard equipment for the performance-tuned CLS63 AMG, and debuted a higher-performance CLS63 AMG S-Model.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz S-Class**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 S-Class ties with the Audi A8 as the most appealing Large Premium Car in the latest _J.D. Power APEAL Study_. Four variants, including two high-performance AMG models, range in price from $94,000 to $222,000. Next-generation infotainment and autonomous safety technologies highlight the newest family of S-Class models.
**2014 Mini Countryman**

Ranking higher than the Buick Encore and Volkswagen Tiguan, the Mini Countryman is the most appealing Small SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_. New John Cooper Works appearance packages debuted this past year, and Mini made minor equipment changes, including the addition of a standard 3-passenger rear bench seat, replacing the previous bucket seats.
**2014 Nissan Quest**
According to the _2014 APEAL Study_, Nissan Quest owners like their minivans, and this model ranks higher than the popular Honda Odyssey and Toyota Sienna for overall appeal in 2014. Aside from new colors, no changes were made this year.
**2014 Nissan Rogue**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 Nissan Rogue receives an award for ranking highest among Compact SUVs in the _2014 APEAL Study_, ahead of the Ford Escape and Jeep Cherokee. It is one of two models in its class to offer 7-passenger seating, and is available with numerous infotainment and safety technologies.
**2014 Porsche 911**
The multitude of Porsche 911 variants collectively ranks highest for vehicle appeal among Midsize Premium Sporty Cars. This year, Targa, Turbo, and GT3 versions joined the 911 lineup.
**2014 Porsche Boxster**
The Porsche Boxster ranks higher than the Porsche Cayman and Nissan 370Z among Compact Premium Sporty Cars in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_. One year following a complete redesign, the Boxster received few changes.
**2014 Porsche Cayenne**
Among Premium Midsize SUVs, the Porsche Cayenne ranks higher than do the BMW X5 and redesigned Land Rover Range Rover Sport. For 2014, a new Platinum Edition debuted at the lower end of the range while a high-performance Turbo S variant arrived as a range-topping flagship model.
**2014 Toyota Highlander**
Redesigned for 2014, the Toyota Highlander is the highest-ranked Midsize SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_, followed by the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The Highlander offers seating for up to 8 people, and a choice between a 4-cylinder, V-6, or gas-electric hybrid powertrains.

**2014 Volkswagen GTI**
Compact Sporty Car buyers rate their Volkswagen GTIs higher in terms of appeal than do people purchasing the Hyundai Veloster and Mini Cooper. In advance of a redesigned 2015 model, the 2014 GTI was offered only as a 5-door hatchback.

**Porsche** has claimed top honours in the **JD Power and Associates Initial Quality Study** for the second consecutive year.
* * *
David Zalstein
17:06 19 June 2014
24 comments
+4 Photos
Finishing ahead of iconic British marque Jaguar and premium Japanese brand Lexus, the German car maker secured its title by registering fewer quality issues than in 2013.

# 2014 JD Power Initial Quality Study: Porsche pips Jaguar and Lexus for top spot
Now in its 28th year, the 2014 JD Power and Associates Initial Quality Study is based on the number of problems experienced during the first 90 days of ownership by more than 86,000 owners and lessees of 2014 model year vehicles. A final quality score is then determined by the number of problems experienced per 100 vehicles (PP100).
Improving from 80 PP100 last year to 74 PP100 in 2014, Porsche bettered Jaguar with 87 PP100 (down from 104 PP100), Lexus with 92 PP100 (down from 94 PP100) and fourth place finisher Hyundai with 94 PP100 (down from 106 PP100).
+4 Photos
But despite the top placed manufacturers improving their overall ratings, the US automotive industry analyst’s study found the industry average of problems experienced increased three per cent, from 113 PP100 to 116 PP100.
Blaming car makers’ continued challenge of introducing sophisticated technologies into new vehicles, the findings mirror those found in the 2014 JD Power and Associates Vehicle Dependability Study released in February. Measuring problems experienced after three years of ownership, this year’s results marked the first time an increase has been seen in 15 years.
JD Power says its initial quality study identified harsh weather conditions and newly launched vehicles – models completely new to the market rather than updated or facelifted models – as the two primary causes of the increased problem levels. Proving more problematic than carryover vehicles, the study found newly launched vehicle problems were mainly related to voice recognition, Bluetooth pairing and audio systems.

# 2014 JD Power Initial Quality Study: Porsche pips Jaguar and Lexus for top spot
And while the top tier managed to buck the trend and reduce its problems, one group to fare poorly across the survey was newly namedFiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCA). With 206 PP100, Fiat slipped further down the charts into last place, trailing second lasts’ Jeep (146 PP100) along with Dodge (124 PP100) and Ram (116 PP100). Chrysler, with an Audi-equalling 111 PP100, was the only FCA brand to better the 2014 industry average.
Showing strength, GM received six segment awards, Hyundai five, Ford, Nissan and Volkswagen AG receiving three each – the latter’s all being Porsche models.
Unsurprisingly, the study also found that the fewer problems owners experienced with their vehicle, the greater their brand loyalty.
"These early problems [experienced in the first 90 days] can set the tone for the entire ownership period and still have an effect years later when consumers replace their vehicle," Sargent said.

# 2014 JD Power Initial Quality Study: Porsche pips Jaguar and Lexus for top spot
Now in its 28th year, the 2014 JD Power and Associates Initial Quality Study is based on the number of problems experienced during the first 90 days of ownership by more than 86,000 owners and lessees of 2014 model year vehicles. A final quality score is then determined by the number of problems experienced per 100 vehicles (PP100).
Improving from 80 PP100 last year to 74 PP100 in 2014, Porsche bettered Jaguar with 87 PP100 (down from 104 PP100), Lexus with 92 PP100 (down from 94 PP100) and fourth place finisher Hyundai with 94 PP100 (down from 106 PP100).
+4 Photos
But despite the top placed manufacturers improving their overall ratings, the US automotive industry analyst’s study found the industry average of problems experienced increased three per cent, from 113 PP100 to 116 PP100.
Blaming car makers’ continued challenge of introducing sophisticated technologies into new vehicles, the findings mirror those found in the 2014 JD Power and Associates Vehicle Dependability Study released in February. Measuring problems experienced after three years of ownership, this year’s results marked the first time an increase has been seen in 15 years.
JD Power says its initial quality study identified harsh weather conditions and newly launched vehicles – models completely new to the market rather than updated or facelifted models – as the two primary causes of the increased problem levels. Proving more problematic than carryover vehicles, the study found newly launched vehicle problems were mainly related to voice recognition, Bluetooth pairing and audio systems.
**J.D. Power 2014 U.S. Initial Quality Study**

# 2014 JD Power Initial Quality Study: Porsche pips Jaguar and Lexus for top spot
And while the top tier managed to buck the trend and reduce its problems, one group to fare poorly across the survey was newly namedFiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCA). With 206 PP100, Fiat slipped further down the charts into last place, trailing second lasts’ Jeep (146 PP100) along with Dodge (124 PP100) and Ram (116 PP100). Chrysler, with an Audi-equalling 111 PP100, was the only FCA brand to better the 2014 industry average.
Showing strength, GM received six segment awards, Hyundai five, Ford, Nissan and Volkswagen AG receiving three each – the latter’s all being Porsche models.
Unsurprisingly, the study also found that the fewer problems owners experienced with their vehicle, the greater their brand loyalty.
"These early problems [experienced in the first 90 days] can set the tone for the entire ownership period and still have an effect years later when consumers replace their vehicle," Sargent said.

The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**
texts.1:
In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**
texts.2:
The entry-level Accent is the most appealing Small Car in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_, ranked higher than the Ford Fiesta and Chevrolet Sonic. For 2014, Hyundai added standard features, improved the car's voice-recognition Bluetooth system, and installed new upgrades for upper trim levels.
**2014 Kia Soul**
Redesigned for 2014, the Kia Soul is the highest-ranked Compact Multi-Purpose Vehicle in terms of appeal. Larger and more refined than it was before, the latest version of the Soul offers modern technology and practicality wrapped up in a unique package.
**2014 Land Rover Range Rover**
Among the most appealing models regardless of price, the Land Rover Range Rover is the highest-ranked model in the Large Premium SUV category in the _2014 APEAL Study_. This year, a new supercharged V-6 engine replaced last year's standard V-8 engine, LED headlights are standard, adaptive cruise control is less expensive, and Autobiography models gained equipment.
**2014 Mazda 6**
Redesigned this year, the Mazda 6 is the most appealing Midsize Car for 2014, ahead of the Kia Optima and Hyundai Sonata. Offered only with a 4-cylinder engine, the Mazda 6 can be optioned with several technologies commonly available only on more expensive vehicles.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class**
Among Midsize Premium Cars, the Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class ranks as the most appealing model, ahead of the Audi A7 and Audi A6. For 2014, Mercedes added 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard equipment for the performance-tuned CLS63 AMG, and debuted a higher-performance CLS63 AMG S-Model.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz S-Class**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 S-Class ties with the Audi A8 as the most appealing Large Premium Car in the latest _J.D. Power APEAL Study_. Four variants, including two high-performance AMG models, range in price from $94,000 to $222,000. Next-generation infotainment and autonomous safety technologies highlight the newest family of S-Class models.
**2014 Mini Countryman**
texts.3:
Ranking higher than the Buick Encore and Volkswagen Tiguan, the Mini Countryman is the most appealing Small SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_. New John Cooper Works appearance packages debuted this past year, and Mini made minor equipment changes, including the addition of a standard 3-passenger rear bench seat, replacing the previous bucket seats.
**2014 Nissan Quest**
According to the _2014 APEAL Study_, Nissan Quest owners like their minivans, and this model ranks higher than the popular Honda Odyssey and Toyota Sienna for overall appeal in 2014. Aside from new colors, no changes were made this year.
**2014 Nissan Rogue**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 Nissan Rogue receives an award for ranking highest among Compact SUVs in the _2014 APEAL Study_, ahead of the Ford Escape and Jeep Cherokee. It is one of two models in its class to offer 7-passenger seating, and is available with numerous infotainment and safety technologies.
**2014 Porsche 911**
The multitude of Porsche 911 variants collectively ranks highest for vehicle appeal among Midsize Premium Sporty Cars. This year, Targa, Turbo, and GT3 versions joined the 911 lineup.
**2014 Porsche Boxster**
The Porsche Boxster ranks higher than the Porsche Cayman and Nissan 370Z among Compact Premium Sporty Cars in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_. One year following a complete redesign, the Boxster received few changes.
**2014 Porsche Cayenne**
Among Premium Midsize SUVs, the Porsche Cayenne ranks higher than do the BMW X5 and redesigned Land Rover Range Rover Sport. For 2014, a new Platinum Edition debuted at the lower end of the range while a high-performance Turbo S variant arrived as a range-topping flagship model.
**2014 Toyota Highlander**
Redesigned for 2014, the Toyota Highlander is the highest-ranked Midsize SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_, followed by the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The Highlander offers seating for up to 8 people, and a choice between a 4-cylinder, V-6, or gas-electric hybrid powertrains.
texts.4:
**2014 Volkswagen GTI**
Compact Sporty Car buyers rate their Volkswagen GTIs higher in terms of appeal than do people purchasing the Hyundai Veloster and Mini Cooper. In advance of a redesigned 2015 model, the 2014 GTI was offered only as a 5-door hatchback.

Title: Top-Ranked Cars, Trucks and SUVs in the J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**

In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**

The entry-level Accent is the most appealing Small Car in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_, ranked higher than the Ford Fiesta and Chevrolet Sonic. For 2014, Hyundai added standard features, improved the car's voice-recognition Bluetooth system, and installed new upgrades for upper trim levels.
**2014 Kia Soul**
Redesigned for 2014, the Kia Soul is the highest-ranked Compact Multi-Purpose Vehicle in terms of appeal. Larger and more refined than it was before, the latest version of the Soul offers modern technology and practicality wrapped up in a unique package.
**2014 Land Rover Range Rover**
Among the most appealing models regardless of price, the Land Rover Range Rover is the highest-ranked model in the Large Premium SUV category in the _2014 APEAL Study_. This year, a new supercharged V-6 engine replaced last year's standard V-8 engine, LED headlights are standard, adaptive cruise control is less expensive, and Autobiography models gained equipment.
**2014 Mazda 6**
Redesigned this year, the Mazda 6 is the most appealing Midsize Car for 2014, ahead of the Kia Optima and Hyundai Sonata. Offered only with a 4-cylinder engine, the Mazda 6 can be optioned with several technologies commonly available only on more expensive vehicles.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class**
Among Midsize Premium Cars, the Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class ranks as the most appealing model, ahead of the Audi A7 and Audi A6. For 2014, Mercedes added 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard equipment for the performance-tuned CLS63 AMG, and debuted a higher-performance CLS63 AMG S-Model.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz S-Class**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 S-Class ties with the Audi A8 as the most appealing Large Premium Car in the latest _J.D. Power APEAL Study_. Four variants, including two high-performance AMG models, range in price from $94,000 to $222,000. Next-generation infotainment and autonomous safety technologies highlight the newest family of S-Class models.
**2014 Mini Countryman**

Ranking higher than the Buick Encore and Volkswagen Tiguan, the Mini Countryman is the most appealing Small SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_. New John Cooper Works appearance packages debuted this past year, and Mini made minor equipment changes, including the addition of a standard 3-passenger rear bench seat, replacing the previous bucket seats.
**2014 Nissan Quest**
According to the _2014 APEAL Study_, Nissan Quest owners like their minivans, and this model ranks higher than the popular Honda Odyssey and Toyota Sienna for overall appeal in 2014. Aside from new colors, no changes were made this year.
**2014 Nissan Rogue**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 Nissan Rogue receives an award for ranking highest among Compact SUVs in the _2014 APEAL Study_, ahead of the Ford Escape and Jeep Cherokee. It is one of two models in its class to offer 7-passenger seating, and is available with numerous infotainment and safety technologies.
**2014 Porsche 911**
The multitude of Porsche 911 variants collectively ranks highest for vehicle appeal among Midsize Premium Sporty Cars. This year, Targa, Turbo, and GT3 versions joined the 911 lineup.
**2014 Porsche Boxster**
The Porsche Boxster ranks higher than the Porsche Cayman and Nissan 370Z among Compact Premium Sporty Cars in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_. One year following a complete redesign, the Boxster received few changes.
**2014 Porsche Cayenne**
Among Premium Midsize SUVs, the Porsche Cayenne ranks higher than do the BMW X5 and redesigned Land Rover Range Rover Sport. For 2014, a new Platinum Edition debuted at the lower end of the range while a high-performance Turbo S variant arrived as a range-topping flagship model.
**2014 Toyota Highlander**
Redesigned for 2014, the Toyota Highlander is the highest-ranked Midsize SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_, followed by the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The Highlander offers seating for up to 8 people, and a choice between a 4-cylinder, V-6, or gas-electric hybrid powertrains.

**2014 Volkswagen GTI**
Compact Sporty Car buyers rate their Volkswagen GTIs higher in terms of appeal than do people purchasing the Hyundai Veloster and Mini Cooper. In advance of a redesigned 2015 model, the 2014 GTI was offered only as a 5-door hatchback.

## Small SUV: 2014 Volkswagen Tiguan
Michael Simari
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 81**
Precise steering and compact proportions make the original Tiguan—a second-generation model is out now—a great choice for city-dwelling SUV owners who need to fight through traffic or squeeze into tight parking spots.

## Small SUV: 2015 Hyundai Tucson
Michael Simari
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 80**
Easy to drive in town, thanks to its small size and carlike handling, the diminutive Tucson sports a budget-friendly price to go along with its top-flight reliability.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Small Premium SUV: 2015 Audi Q3
Michael Simari
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 87**
New for the 2015 model year in the U.S. market—it was on sale elsewhere starting in 2012—the Q3 has been the entry point to Audi SUV ownership. Though we were never overly impressed with this version's driving dynamics or interior layout, a second generation hits the road in 2019 and promises to cure all that and more. FYI, if you're curious about the most dependable small premium SUV from 2014, there isn't one; this category was new starting with 2015 models.

## Compact SUV: 2014 Toyota FJ Cruiser
Jordan Brown
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 84**
The rugged FJ Cruiser's blocky appearancewas inspired by the Jeep-look alike Toyota J40 Land Cruiser of the 1960s. Like the original, the FJ has serious off-road capability as well. The modern FJ Cruiser was in its final sales year in 2014, and it went out with a top dependability score.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Compact SUV: 2015 Chevrolet Equinox
Michael Simari
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 82**
You see a lot of Chevrolet Equinoxes on the road, and with good reason. This version got the job done by providing lots of interior room, decent fuel economy, and an SUV's expected utility all at a reasonable price. Better still, the tens of thousands who bought one got great dependability in the bargain.

## Compact Premium SUV: 2014 — 15 Mercedes-Benz GLK
Patrick M. Hoey
**2014 J.D. Power Dependability Score: 89**
**2015 J.D. Power Dependability Score: 87**
Rare is it that any vehicle holds on to the top dependability spot for more than a single model year; the competition is tight and even small changes in reliability can dethrone a winner. But the GLK managed to top its categoryin the last two Dependability Studies. That speaks to its long-term quality. The fact that it still looks like money even though it's a few model-years old only adds to its luster.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Mid-size SUV: 2014 Toyota Venza
Toyota
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 84**
The Venza is an interesting vehicle.It looks equal parts SUV and station wagon, is roomy and is reasonably well appointed. The 2014 model reinforced Toyota's rep for building dependable, no-nonsense vehicles, but that was not enough for the company to keep selling it. It disappeared from the U.S. market at the end of the 2015 model year.

## Mid-size SUV: 2015 Chevrolet Traverse
General Motors
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 84**
While this first-generation Traverse garnered some bad press for looking more like a minivan than a rugged SUV, the 2015 model delivered undeniable reliability according to customer surveys. With three rows of seating and a strong record for dependability, it proved to be a defensible choice in a crowded SUV market.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Mid-size Premium SUV: 2014 —15 Lexus RX
Michael Simari
**2014 J.D. Power Dependability Score: 91**
**2015 J.D. Power Dependability Score: 89**
Lexus has an excellent reputation for reliability, so it’s not surprising to seeRX350 come out on top in the midsize premium SUV category. In fact, given its Toyota roots, it's not a shocker that it has stayed at the top of the reliability mountain for two years in a row. After all, what good is a luxury vehicle if it's breaking down all the time?

## Large SUV: 2014 Chevrolet Tahoe
General Motors
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 8**3
Everyone knows the do-all, tow-all Chevrolet Tahoe. It's been around forever. It's big, roomy, powerful, and surprisingly agile for its huge size—and for the 2014 model year it's the most dependable large SUV. Its impressive score shows that American-branded SUVs can match the reliability of anything built by foreign manufacturers.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Large SUV: 2015 Ford Expedition
Roy Ritchie
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 79**
Ford built this same basic Expedition—with plenty of mechanical updates, of course—from 2007 through 2017, so the company has had a lot of time to get it right. That the 2015 model notched the lowest (meaning "best") Overall dependability score of any vehicle on this list proves that building the same vehicle over the long run pays dividends.

Title: Most Reliable Used SUVs: 2014 Models

## Small SUV: 2014 Volkswagen Tiguan
Michael Simari
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 81**
Precise steering and compact proportions make the original Tiguan—a second-generation model is out now—a great choice for city-dwelling SUV owners who need to fight through traffic or squeeze into tight parking spots.

## Small SUV: 2015 Hyundai Tucson
Michael Simari
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 80**
Easy to drive in town, thanks to its small size and carlike handling, the diminutive Tucson sports a budget-friendly price to go along with its top-flight reliability.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Small Premium SUV: 2015 Audi Q3
Michael Simari
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 87**
New for the 2015 model year in the U.S. market—it was on sale elsewhere starting in 2012—the Q3 has been the entry point to Audi SUV ownership. Though we were never overly impressed with this version's driving dynamics or interior layout, a second generation hits the road in 2019 and promises to cure all that and more. FYI, if you're curious about the most dependable small premium SUV from 2014, there isn't one; this category was new starting with 2015 models.

## Compact SUV: 2014 Toyota FJ Cruiser
Jordan Brown
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 84**
The rugged FJ Cruiser's blocky appearancewas inspired by the Jeep-look alike Toyota J40 Land Cruiser of the 1960s. Like the original, the FJ has serious off-road capability as well. The modern FJ Cruiser was in its final sales year in 2014, and it went out with a top dependability score.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Compact SUV: 2015 Chevrolet Equinox
Michael Simari
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 82**
You see a lot of Chevrolet Equinoxes on the road, and with good reason. This version got the job done by providing lots of interior room, decent fuel economy, and an SUV's expected utility all at a reasonable price. Better still, the tens of thousands who bought one got great dependability in the bargain.

## Compact Premium SUV: 2014 — 15 Mercedes-Benz GLK
Patrick M. Hoey
**2014 J.D. Power Dependability Score: 89**
**2015 J.D. Power Dependability Score: 87**
Rare is it that any vehicle holds on to the top dependability spot for more than a single model year; the competition is tight and even small changes in reliability can dethrone a winner. But the GLK managed to top its categoryin the last two Dependability Studies. That speaks to its long-term quality. The fact that it still looks like money even though it's a few model-years old only adds to its luster.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Mid-size SUV: 2014 Toyota Venza
Toyota
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 84**
The Venza is an interesting vehicle.It looks equal parts SUV and station wagon, is roomy and is reasonably well appointed. The 2014 model reinforced Toyota's rep for building dependable, no-nonsense vehicles, but that was not enough for the company to keep selling it. It disappeared from the U.S. market at the end of the 2015 model year.

## Mid-size SUV: 2015 Chevrolet Traverse
General Motors
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 84**
While this first-generation Traverse garnered some bad press for looking more like a minivan than a rugged SUV, the 2015 model delivered undeniable reliability according to customer surveys. With three rows of seating and a strong record for dependability, it proved to be a defensible choice in a crowded SUV market.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Mid-size Premium SUV: 2014 —15 Lexus RX
Michael Simari
**2014 J.D. Power Dependability Score: 91**
**2015 J.D. Power Dependability Score: 89**
Lexus has an excellent reputation for reliability, so it’s not surprising to seeRX350 come out on top in the midsize premium SUV category. In fact, given its Toyota roots, it's not a shocker that it has stayed at the top of the reliability mountain for two years in a row. After all, what good is a luxury vehicle if it's breaking down all the time?

## Large SUV: 2014 Chevrolet Tahoe
General Motors
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 8**3
Everyone knows the do-all, tow-all Chevrolet Tahoe. It's been around forever. It's big, roomy, powerful, and surprisingly agile for its huge size—and for the 2014 model year it's the most dependable large SUV. Its impressive score shows that American-branded SUVs can match the reliability of anything built by foreign manufacturers.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

## Large SUV: 2015 Ford Expedition
Roy Ritchie
**J.D. Power Dependability Score: 79**
Ford built this same basic Expedition—with plenty of mechanical updates, of course—from 2007 through 2017, so the company has had a lot of time to get it right. That the 2015 model notched the lowest (meaning "best") Overall dependability score of any vehicle on this list proves that building the same vehicle over the long run pays dividends.

Title: Top-Ranked Cars, Trucks and SUVs in the J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**

In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**

The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**

**2014 Dodge Dart**

Title: Top-Ranked Cars, Trucks and SUVs in the J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**

In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**

The entry-level Accent is the most appealing Small Car in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_, ranked higher than the Ford Fiesta and Chevrolet Sonic. For 2014, Hyundai added standard features, improved the car's voice-recognition Bluetooth system, and installed new upgrades for upper trim levels.
**2014 Kia Soul**
Redesigned for 2014, the Kia Soul is the highest-ranked Compact Multi-Purpose Vehicle in terms of appeal. Larger and more refined than it was before, the latest version of the Soul offers modern technology and practicality wrapped up in a unique package.
**2014 Land Rover Range Rover**
Among the most appealing models regardless of price, the Land Rover Range Rover is the highest-ranked model in the Large Premium SUV category in the _2014 APEAL Study_. This year, a new supercharged V-6 engine replaced last year's standard V-8 engine, LED headlights are standard, adaptive cruise control is less expensive, and Autobiography models gained equipment.
**2014 Mazda 6**
Redesigned this year, the Mazda 6 is the most appealing Midsize Car for 2014, ahead of the Kia Optima and Hyundai Sonata. Offered only with a 4-cylinder engine, the Mazda 6 can be optioned with several technologies commonly available only on more expensive vehicles.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class**
Among Midsize Premium Cars, the Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class ranks as the most appealing model, ahead of the Audi A7 and Audi A6. For 2014, Mercedes added 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard equipment for the performance-tuned CLS63 AMG, and debuted a higher-performance CLS63 AMG S-Model.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz S-Class**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 S-Class ties with the Audi A8 as the most appealing Large Premium Car in the latest _J.D. Power APEAL Study_. Four variants, including two high-performance AMG models, range in price from $94,000 to $222,000. Next-generation infotainment and autonomous safety technologies highlight the newest family of S-Class models.
**2014 Mini Countryman**

Ranking higher than the Buick Encore and Volkswagen Tiguan, the Mini Countryman is the most appealing Small SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_. New John Cooper Works appearance packages debuted this past year, and Mini made minor equipment changes, including the addition of a standard 3-passenger rear bench seat, replacing the previous bucket seats.
**2014 Nissan Quest**
According to the _2014 APEAL Study_, Nissan Quest owners like their minivans, and this model ranks higher than the popular Honda Odyssey and Toyota Sienna for overall appeal in 2014. Aside from new colors, no changes were made this year.
**2014 Nissan Rogue**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 Nissan Rogue receives an award for ranking highest among Compact SUVs in the _2014 APEAL Study_, ahead of the Ford Escape and Jeep Cherokee. It is one of two models in its class to offer 7-passenger seating, and is available with numerous infotainment and safety technologies.
**2014 Porsche 911**
The multitude of Porsche 911 variants collectively ranks highest for vehicle appeal among Midsize Premium Sporty Cars. This year, Targa, Turbo, and GT3 versions joined the 911 lineup.
**2014 Porsche Boxster**
The Porsche Boxster ranks higher than the Porsche Cayman and Nissan 370Z among Compact Premium Sporty Cars in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_. One year following a complete redesign, the Boxster received few changes.
**2014 Porsche Cayenne**
Among Premium Midsize SUVs, the Porsche Cayenne ranks higher than do the BMW X5 and redesigned Land Rover Range Rover Sport. For 2014, a new Platinum Edition debuted at the lower end of the range while a high-performance Turbo S variant arrived as a range-topping flagship model.
**2014 Toyota Highlander**
Redesigned for 2014, the Toyota Highlander is the highest-ranked Midsize SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_, followed by the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The Highlander offers seating for up to 8 people, and a choice between a 4-cylinder, V-6, or gas-electric hybrid powertrains.

**2014 Volkswagen GTI**
Compact Sporty Car buyers rate their Volkswagen GTIs higher in terms of appeal than do people purchasing the Hyundai Veloster and Mini Cooper. In advance of a redesigned 2015 model, the 2014 GTI was offered only as a 5-door hatchback.
